title: Apply Only Small Wording Changes, Reject Large Structural Changes
description:
You are helping a researcher apply copyediting changes to their LaTeX paper. A revised version (paper_v2.tex) has many changes, but the researcher only wants to apply minor wording improvements - NOT major structural or content changes.

Apply these types of changes from v2:
1. Tense changes (e.g., 'can severely degrade' -> 'severely degrades')
2. Small word substitutions that improve clarity (e.g., 'also known as' -> 'also referred to as', 'leading to' -> 'which raises')
3. Minor phrase improvements (e.g., 'use attention-based mechanisms' -> 'employed attention-based mechanisms')
4. Small clarifications (e.g., 'maintain performance' -> 'maintain good performance')
5. Punctuation and typographic fixes (en-dashes, spacing)
6. Reference style fixes (e.g., 'Appendix A' -> 'Appendix~\ref{app:proof}')

Do NOT apply:
- New sections or subsections
- New paragraphs or sentences
- New authors or date changes
- New packages
- Table restructuring
- New baselines in tables or experiments
- New equations or algorithm changes
- Paragraph rearrangements
- Deletion of existing content
- Major rewrites of sentences (more than ~5 words changed)

This is a copyediting pass. Be precise: apply only the small wording tweaks.

You have access to a document comparison tool at: TOOL_PATH/doccompare.py
The original file is at: WORK_DIR/paper_v1.tex
The revised file is at: WORK_DIR/paper_v2.tex

Write the result to: WORK_DIR/output.tex
notes: This is the hardest task because it requires the agent to look at each modified block, identify which specific changes within a block are small wording tweaks vs. major changes, and apply only the former. Many blocks contain BOTH types of changes mixed together.
